---
title: "Layout Modeling Check"
description: "Check from a layout repository that SCGSim can model a layout, before any simulation is set up."
scgsim-kind: "contract"
scgsim-status: "CONVERGING"
scgsim-id: "docs/layout-modeling-check"
---

`simulation_drc()` tells a layout repository whether SCGSim can model its
layout. It runs the same preparation and geometry build that
`EigenmodeSim.mesh()` runs, then stops before meshing. A layout that cannot be
modeled is refused with the error the build raises, and a layout that can be
modeled returns `None`.

## Call it while drawing and in tests

The check needs the layout Component and the PDK data a simulation would use:
the layer stack and the material records. SCGSim does not depend on a PDK, so
the layout repository passes them in.

```python
from scgsim.palace import simulation_drc


def test_the_layout_can_be_modeled():
    simulation_drc(
        component,
        layer_stack=layer_stack,
        material_records=material_records,
        surface_epr_specs=surface_epr_specs,
    )
```

Call it from the repository's tests and while the layout is being drawn. Pass
`surface_epr_specs` when the layout will be used for Surface EPR: the specs are
the ones [`set_surface_epr`](specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins)
takes, and their margins are cut into the geometry as bands, so a layout that
cannot carry them is refused here too. For an assembly, pass `instances` as
`{"chip/device": reference, ...}`, as `GeometryPlan.register_instance` takes
them; the plan's root is named `chip`.

The check builds the geometry and does not mesh or solve, so it can be repeated
as the layout changes. It stops at the first refusal. Read the message, fix the
layout, and run it again. The [error archive](errors.qmd) records diagnostics
seen in practice.

## What the check uses

The settings are fixed:

- Route B;
- every authored port;
- no nets;
- zero coupon padding.

`simulation_drc()` writes into a temporary folder and removes it. It adds no
rules of its own and no report type, so the error is the one `mesh()` would
raise for the same layout and settings.

::: {.callout-note title="What a pass means"}
`simulation_drc()` only checks that the layout can be modeled directly. It does
not promise that nets, Electrostatic terminals, Route A, junctions, lumped
supports or a vacuum region will work. To check a specific simulation, run that
simulation's own `mesh()`.
:::

AEDT is outside this check: its modeling runs inside AEDT, not through SGB.
